To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Mach waves are emitted by supersonic jets and that the source strength is determined by the mean shear and density fluctuations of the jets.
the Mach wave noise of a supersonic jet is generated in the region where the mean shear and density fluctuations are maximum and that the noise level in this region is independent of jet temperature.
the Mach waves are generated by the interaction of the shear layers and the density fluctuations in the shear layers of the jet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed experimental investigation of the far field acoustic characteristics of supersonic jets over a wide temperature range.
the generation and propagation of sound in the atmosphere.
the development and use of a computer program to calculate the acoustic field generated by a supersonic jet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mach waves are generated by the shear in the jet and that they are emitted at angles that depend upon the local Mach angle.
the sound generated in supersonic jets arises from two distinct sources.
the noise of a supersonic jet is due to the turbulent mixing and the resulting compressions and expansions of the hot and cold streams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sound generation is due to the turbulent mixing of the jet with the surrounding air, the turbulent shear layer of the jet, and the turbulence within the core of the jet.
the Mach wave is a result of the mixing of the cold and hot streams and is not associated with the jet boundary layer or shock waves.
sound is generated in a jet flow by the mixing of the streams and that the strength of this sound is determined by the density fluctuations in the jet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is not necessary to have a shock wave in order to produce Mach waves.
the noise in supersonic jets can be predicted from the mean flow and the density fluctuations.
the Mach wave emission from supersonic jets is a consequence of jet mixing, which in turn is a result of the shear layer instability.
